summary: Iteration 21 backend testing complete — 19/19 tests passed (100%). Validated /api/system/subscription/verify hardening with the new play_verifier module. Fallback trust-mode confirmed: with no GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON/PATH env, verify returns is_premium=true, correct plan mapping (monthly/yearly/lifetime), and source='play_billing_unverified'; MongoDB subscriptions collection persists with source='play_billing_unverified' and /subscription/restore returns the same source. Validation errors covered: 401 user_id_required (missing X-User-Id), 400 purchase_token_required (empty token), 400 unknown_product (bad SKU). play_verifier module tested directly: _build_client() returns None with a WARNING log when no env is set; verify_purchase() returns None (fallback). Malformed GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON ('{not-valid-json') → _build_client() logs error, returns None on both first and cached second call, no crash; verify_purchase falls back to None gracefully. Configured mode simulated by monkeypatching _build_client to a fake androidpublisher client — subscriptionsv2 path returns VerifiedPurchase(entitled=True, state=SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_ACTIVE, expiry_iso preserved, order_id captured); products path auto-acknowledges (ack called exactly once) and returns state='PURCHASED'; HttpError from Play API is translated to ValueError('play_api_error:400') which system_routes wraps into HTTP 400. Regression on /api/system/pricing (all fields present), /api/system/quota, /api/system/rewarded/claim (grant + premium_no_bonus_needed), /api/legal/privacy, /api/legal/data-deletion — all 200 OK, identical behaviour to iteration_20.
critical_code_review_comments: play_verifier._client_error latches on FIRST failure and prevents _build_client() from ever retrying, even after env vars are added at runtime. If ops rotates a service-account key without restarting, the process is stuck in fallback mode. Consider exposing a reset() helper or checking env-change on each call.

system_routes.subscription_verify catches broad Exception and returns 500 'verify_internal_error'. Because pv._build_client() swallows its own failures and returns None, this path only fires for truly unexpected bugs — good, but consider logging the payload's product_id (never the purchase_token) to help ops triage.

verify_purchase() Auto-ack on subscriptions calls client.purchases().subscriptions().acknowledge(...) but the subscriptionsv2 GET is used elsewhere. The v1 acknowledge endpoint is still valid, but Google recommends using subscriptionsv2 uniformly — consider migrating for consistency.

In fallback (unverified) mode the server still writes purchase_token to Mongo. If purchase_token is ever considered PII/secret in your threat model, at least hash it before storing. Not blocking for launch.

Test regression noticed: older records from previous iterations still have source='play_billing' (pre-hardening). New writes correctly use 'play_billing_unverified'. Since restore sorts by granted_at desc, a user who verified twice (once pre-hardening, once post) will see 'play_billing' returned — not a bug, but worth mentioning in the audit dashboard docs.
test_credentials: None — X-User-Id headers use unique UUIDs per test.
seed_data_creation: MongoDB subscriptions collection: uids prefixed qa-verify-fallback-*, qa-verify-restore-*, qa-quota-*, qa-rw-*. Idempotent across re-runs (upsert by uid+purchase_token).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Subscription-verify hardening is production-safe for fallback mode. The Play API branch is exercised only through monkeypatched fake clients — end-to-end sandbox verification requires a real Google service account JSON in GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON plus a sandbox purchase token from Play Console internal test track. If the next iteration wires that in, extend test_verify_purchase_uses_fake_client_* with real integration and add a status.expires_at parse test to ensure Play's RFC3339 expiryTime survives the round-trip.
rca of the issue: N/A — no failures. Hardening behaves as spec'd.
